title: Designed, then built, then shipped
subtitle: AI products in production, prototypes in real code, and a design system that lives as an API

cv.label: Download CV (PDF)
cv.note: Tailored for the Design Lead role

bio.short: I design software and I build it. At Bibel TV an AI support copilot, an AI fundraising system, a token API and a color engine are live. An engineering agency outside the company ships from my prototype code. With Ninox's founders I designed the prompt-to-database onboarding that became their public AI beta.
bio.long:
The last year at Bibel TV went into AI that runs in production. The support copilot drafts replies to viewer letters in the handbook's own wording. A restricted-topic list sits in the system prompt, and every send decision stays with a person. The fundraising ecosystem I built solo: a performance analysis of past letters, a Claude Project that asks clarifying questions before it writes, a web prototype, and a production Claude skill. Its output spans in-app notifications, web banners and video scripts.

I prototype the app redesign in real code. Web first, then a native Android app in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose against real and self-built APIs. The agency that builds the app sits outside the company, and a teardown of the shipped build found 91.8% of my token fields in it. The design system behind that lives as an API in four tiers, with Storybook as the source of truth. A color engine in OKLCH holds contrast in light and dark. Product managers and product owners shape features there without a design team beside them. So I also hold product management and product ownership for the redesign.

In summer 2025, as a consultant, I designed Ninox's prompt-to-database onboarding with the CEO and technical co-founder. The generated schema renders into the real data-model editor beside the chat, because chat alone could not carry a real schema and the user had to be able to own it. Before all that I led design at Head and Director level for a decade. On my own time I build aperto.bible, open-source Bible translation tooling with an AI content pipeline and an evaluation harness I designed and directed. And Selah, a Mac app on the Mac App Store. I live in Berlin, German native, English C2.

context.emphasis: Lead with AI products he built that are live in production, and with prototypes in real code that an external agency ships from, using the measured 91.8% teardown figure. Show the Ninox prompt-to-database pattern as the novel UX pattern: direct manipulation beside chat. Pair the builder evidence with the decade of design leadership. Berlin, on site, no relocation.
